hook.line: Mariana cannot print what she cannot prove. So the news has a toolkit for "someone says it, but I will not say who". Neighbours at the café use the same tricks.
hook.es: Se dice que Altamira ya compró dos edificios.
hook.en: It's said that Altamira has already bought two buildings.

examples.es: Se cree que fue un error.

examples.es: Se dice que Altamira ya compró dos edificios.

rule:
Sometimes nobody knows who did it, or you would rather not say. Spanish has four easy ways to leave the person out.

*Dicen que...* or *Cuentan que...*: "they say". Plain third-person plural, no *ellos*.

*Se dice que...*, *Se cree que...*, *Se sabe que...*: "it's said, believed, known". The verb after *se* stays singular, whatever follows. Newspapers love it.

*Uno* plus a normal verb: "one" or "you" in general, often including yourself.

*La gente* plus a singular verb: *la gente cree*, never *creen*.

None of these names a source. When you have one, add *según*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the impersonal register: the doer is hidden with a plural *dicen*, an impersonal *se*, or a general *uno*.

options: The mayor says they resigned.
They say the mayor resigned.
The mayor said he would resign.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *dicen* or *dice* and type the whole sentence: *___ que Altamira compró el edificio.* (the rumour mill, no one in particular)
yourTurn.answer: Dicen que Altamira compró el edificio.
yourTurn.why: "They say" with no one named is the plural *dicen*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's believed it was a mistake.
yourTurn.answer: Se cree que fue un error.
yourTurn.why: "It's believed" is *se cree que*, with the verb singular.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: People think the café is going to close.
yourTurn.answer: La gente cree que el café va a cerrar.
accept: La gente piensa que el café va a cerrar.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: They say the owner left the country.
yourTurn.answer: Dicen que el dueño salió del país.
accept: Cuentan que el dueño salió del país.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: One can't know everything. (anyone, in general)
yourTurn.why: A general "one" is *uno* with an ordinary verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Hide who is saying it, "it's said": *Altamira compró el edificio.*
yourTurn.answer: Se dice que Altamira compró el edificio.
yourTurn.why: Put *se dice que* in front and the claim has no owner.

yourTurn.prompt: Hide who believes it: *Mariana cree que fue un error.*
yourTurn.answer: Se cree que fue un error.
yourTurn.why: Replace the person with *se cree que* and keep the rest.

pitfalls.wrong: La gente creen que el café va a cerrar.
pitfalls.right: La gente cree que el café va a cerrar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *La gente* looks plural in English, but in Spanish it is singular: *cree*.

pitfalls.wrong: Se dicen que el alcalde renunció.
pitfalls.right: Se dice que el alcalde renunció.
pitfalls.why: Almost. In *se dice que* the verb stays singular, because what follows is a whole clause.
Careful. *Dice* is one person speaking; the plural *dicen* is the rumour mill, "they say".

pitfalls.wrong: Se cree de que fue un error.
pitfalls.right: Se cree que fue un error.
pitfalls.why: Almost. There is no *de* before *que* here.

personal: Pass on a rumour you have heard about your town or workplace, using *Dicen que...* or *Se dice que...*.
